title: Stress propagation is not required for patterning but improves adaptation to change

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Stress propagation is not required for patterning but improves adaptation to change

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Across 10 evolved neural cellular automaton tissues, stress signalling was not required to solve the French flag problem (only 1 of 10 died without it), but the tissue that used stress instructively scored significantly better when the target morphology was changed mid-development (p = 0.0312), suggesting that spatial propagation of stress information increases adaptive fitness under perturbation.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Evolution exploits the stress system but anxiolytics do not always have an impact on anatomical homeostasis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For this problem, anatomical homeostasis without stress is possible but exploiting spatial propagation of stress information seems to increase adaptive fitness by improving performance in scenarios where the normal process of morphogenesis is impacted by external perturbations.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Computational results › Evolution exploits the stress system but anxiolytics do not always have an impact on anatomical homeostasis”. Scope: Ten evolved tissues in the 2D neural cellular automaton model

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-08: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.93

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim specifies both a baseline ablation and a perturbation comparison, all reproducible in public code. Limited controller sampling affects generality but not resolvability of the stated result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For all ten controllers, ablate stress signalling during ordinary patterning and during prespecified target changes, then compare survival and accuracy with paired statistics. Replicate the 1-of-10 baseline dependence and the reported adaptive advantage.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The p-value may depend on the chosen target-change scenario.

Ten evolved tissues provide limited power and independence.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Death without stress and accuracy after a target change are defined readouts, and the code can express both interventions. The claim's numbers are properties of ten particular evolutionary outcomes that are not in the repository. A new sample can estimate the rates, but it cannot confirm or refute p = 0.0312 for that sample, and the compute is beyond a quick standard analysis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Evolve or reload ten high-fitness tissues, disable stress, and count how many die, then change the target morphology mid-run and compare the stress-using tissue with the others. One death in ten, plus a higher score for the stress-using tissue under the target change with p near 0.03, would reproduce the claim; many deaths, or no accuracy gap, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ten full ES-HyperNEAT evolutions are a large compute job, and genomes were not released.

The p-value contrasts one stress-using tissue with nine others and will not recur from new seeds.
